title: Write the autopilot operating manual
description:
## What

Write the **autopilot operating manual** — a field guide the autopilot reads on kickoff and references when a situation calls for it — and wire the Autopilot prompt to consult it.

`docs/autopilot-operating-manual.md` (or similar) + an instruction in the Autopilot kickoff/orchestrator prompt (`lib/prompts/autopilot-kickoff.js` / `buildAutopilotKickoff()`) to read it on kickoff and reference the relevant part when a trigger appears. Reference, don't inline — keep the light-orchestrator invariant.

## Why

This is the **autopilot-native, cheaper realisation of the superseded drift-defense epic LIN-289**: the supervisor and evidence-discipline become guide-text read by an agent already positioned to flag, rather than bespoke coded subsystems. Most detection already exists in the per-prompt sensors and the proxy API; the manual is the **judgment layer that ties them together**.

## The specifics that matter (and why)

These are the decisions research won't independently rediscover — hold them; fill in everything else from the track record.

* **Write it human-shaped: intro → how a run normally goes → known issues to watch for.** An onboarding doc, not a flat rulebook. *Why:* you can't recognise trouble without first describing normal, so the happy-path section is load-bearing, not filler.
* **Ground it on altitude.** The autopilot is high (dispatch, watch, decide keep-going/reorient/restart/escalate); the generated prompts do the heavy lifting low; the loop self-corrects across passes. *Why:* most autopilot failures are altitude violations — diving in to fix it itself, or halting the whole run over a local wobble. Altitude is the through-line that ties the parts together.
* **Tolerant operating stance.** Don't halt at the first sign of trouble; watch the *far* edge not the near one (react too late and the cost to unwind has compounded — HAR-527 ended in a 100% boot hang); scale tolerance to reversibility (loose on a prototype branch, tight near merge/Done/anything downstream consumes); light touch, surface-don't-resolve. *Why:* this is exactly where we broke from LIN-289's "interrupt early" bar — the AI can keep going where a human would stop, and that asymmetry is the point.
* **Descriptive, never normative.** It documents how we actually operate and fail; it never redefines "done." Non-autonomy firewall holds.

## Method (high level)

Seed from the design conversation (above) → **research our own track record concretely** — the named failure episodes, not abstractions (`docs/autopilot-experiment.md` runs B1–B4, the autopilot + drift docs, real Linear/git episodes; run the `retro` lens over a real churn cluster for a worked example per known-issue) → write it → wire the prompt to it.

The known-issues to cover are at least: drift (write first — deepest, sets the format), completion-evidence ("\[done\] != done"), orientation/routing at the right altitude, halt-vs-improvise on failure, the human edge / escalation, run-level stop conditions, reversibility guardrails. Each grounded in a **named** episode (e.g. run B4's false-positive `[done]`, run B2's halt-on-infra rule, cancelled LIN-296's wrong-altitude routing), giving a usable keep-going/reorient/restart/escalate calibration.

## Done when

The manual exists and is human-shaped, with the Drift entry complete and the rest at least drafted from named episodes; altitude is the visible through-line; and the Autopilot prompt reads and references it (a dispatched run can be shown consulting the right part on its trigger).

## Out of scope

No new sensor service, scheduler, or auto-remediation — this is documentation + a prompt instruction. A "does the manual change behaviour?" measurement is a separate ticket if wanted.

## Relations

Supersedes LIN-289 (+ LIN-290/291/292/293, closed). Extends the Autopilot work (kickoff generator, orchestrator prompt, periodicals LIN-315).

---

## Research findings (LIN-325 research pass — 2026-06-07)

*Appended by the research pass; the design intent above is held, not revised. Full notes:* `docs/autopilot-operating-manual-research.md`*. Re-grounded at HEAD —* `buildAutopilotKickoff()` *is confirmed the right wiring point and* `docs/autopilot-experiment.md` *still contains B1–B4.*

### Episode → known-issue map (Drift first — deepest, sets the entry format)

Entry format for each: **what it looks like → named episode → keep-going / reorient / restart / escalate.**

1. **Drift** *(write first)* — **HAR-527** boot-hang spiral (A→B→C→D patch graph; retry → 100% hang; fix only existed one altitude up). In-project echo: the `/recommend` 504 misdiagnosis cluster (retro worked-example). Autopilot-native sensor already in the kickoff: the `kind` **trajectory** (research→plan→impl→review = converging; same kind repeating = looping; kind widening = sprawling). *Call:* one locally-correct step → keep going; the sequence repeating/widening → reorient (name the routed-around root) → escalate at the substrate/architecture altitude (the human's).
2. **Completion-evidence (**`[done]` **!= done)** — Run **B4**: a worker posted terminal `[done]` while its rebase-push + comment were still pending (backgrounded the 733-test suite, exited at the session boundary); PR #327 SHA unchanged, no comment — the work landed \~6 min later and the channel never caught up. Secondary: Stage-A Run 4 (clean `cli` retro completed, terminal event never posted). *Call:* `[done]` = 'go verify'; confirm a **change in the external artifact**.
3. **Orientation / routing at the right altitude** — **LIN-296** (Canceled): a recommendation on an epic returned 'implement subtask X'; on the subtask itself returned 'plan' — same work, wrong altitude. *Call:* orient at the altitude of the unit you'll dispatch, not its parent; precedence policy is human-authored.
4. **Halt-vs-improvise on failure** — Run **B2**: `/recommend` 504'd, the orchestrator hand-authored a prompt to keep going (silent workaround, invariant-1 violation) → corrected into the **halt-on-infra-error rule**. *Call:* infra error in your own verbs → halt + surface, never substitute a prompt (distinct from a clean task-level `[failed]`).
5. **Human edge / escalation** — Run **B4** disposition: flagged to the human rather than re-dispatching into a half-applied local rebase; the human supplied the merge pre-auth + the out-of-band observation that broke the stale-channel tie. **⚠ Gap:** a *worker-failure* escalation (clean `[failed]`/stall → `help`) has never been exercised.
6. **Run-level stop conditions** — B3: arc stopped at the verified plan when `/recommend` 504'd 3× (halt rule). Finish lines: scoped run → verified-complete; open-ended walk → runs until it needs you. **⚠ Gap:** no genuinely unattended run (B1–B4 all supervised).
7. **Reversibility guardrails** — Run **B4**: moved the merge gate off the worker (resolve+verify+push-then-stop; orchestrator took the human-authorized merge as a verified action). B2 rationale: Git makes merge-to-main reversible. *Call:* scale tolerance to reversibility (loose on a prototype branch, tight near merge/Done); watch the **far** edge, not the near one (HAR-527: react late and the unwind cost has compounded).

### Recommended manual structure (section level)

Confirms the human-shaped spine; **altitude is the through-line across all three sections**, not its own section.

* **§0 What Autopilot is (intro/onboarding)** — establish the altitude stance (you're high: dispatch/watch/decide; prompts do the heavy lifting low; the loop self-corrects across passes) + tolerant stance + descriptive-not-normative firewall.
* **§1 How a normal run goes (happy path — load-bearing)** — orient → trigger → watch → cross-check → decide → repeat, each beat tagged with the altitude it operates at. Can't recognise trouble without describing normal first.
* **§2 Known issues to watch for** — the seven entries above, **Drift first**, each framed as an altitude question (near-edge wobble = keep going vs far-edge problem = act).

Altitude woven through: the *stance* in §0, the *altitude of each beat* in §1, every failure named as an altitude violation in §2 (diving too low to fix it yourself, or halting too high over a local wobble).

### Wiring approach

Reference, don't inline (light-orchestrator invariant). Autopilot is API-only, so a `docs/` path isn't reachable — but there's a clean precedent: `GET /api/proxy/foreman/playbook` (`routes/proxy.js:3050`) serves `buildForemanPlaybook()` as plain text, and `GET /api/proxy/autopilot/kickoff` serves the kickoff. **Mirror them** with a manual-serving endpoint (e.g. `GET /api/proxy/autopilot/manual`) + a one-line entry in the instructions catalog. Then in `buildAutopilotKickoff()`: add the manual to the **Setup** verb list ('read the operating manual on kickoff'), note in the 'You've run this loop before…' paragraph that the manual expands it, and map triggers → sections (a `done` → completion-evidence; `[stalled?]`/`last tool: Bash` → watch+completion; infra error → halt; looping/widening `kind` → drift; review-raising-direction → human-edge). Both-paths discipline: any kickoff change lands in `lib/prompts/autopilot-kickoff.js` **and** `docs/autopilot-kickoff.md`.

### Surface Assessment

**Surface Assessment: \[yes, implementation can land cleanly\]** — with one small *additive* seam, not a refactor. The kickoff already has natural extension points for 'read this doc on start' (the Setup verb list + the 'You've run this loop before…' paragraph) and clean trigger→section hooks (the existing watch/halt/cross-check/decide steps). The only genuinely-new piece is making the manual reachable by an API-only session: a manual-serving proxy endpoint mirroring the existing `GET /api/proxy/foreman/playbook` + a catalog line — \~10 additive lines against a pattern that already has two such plain-text endpoints. No refactor of the kickoff structure or the proxy required.

### Gaps flagged (real, not papered over)

1. **Worker-failure escalation has no episode** (B2–B4 hit infra-halt + evidence-contradiction only, never `[failed]`→`help`).
2. **No genuinely unattended run** (B1–B4 supervised; B4 needed a human observation to terminate).
3. **The autopilot-native drift sensor has never fired in-loop** (drift grounded historically via HAR-527 + the misdiagnosis cluster, but B1–B4 all converged — the `kind`-trajectory looping/sprawling read is unproven live).

nodes.body:
## Exploration notes — research pass (LIN-325)

Research-only pass. Notes committed to `docs/autopilot-operating-manual-research.md` on branch `claude/lin-325-autopilot-manual-Lv2OM`. The design intent in the description (human-shaped, altitude-grounded, tolerant, descriptive) was held, not relitigated — this pass sourced the substance underneath it.

**Staleness check (re-grounded at HEAD).** Nothing relevant changed since the ticket's `2026-06-07` Created date (only LIN-324's orientation work touched `docs/`). Confirmed at HEAD: `buildAutopilotKickoff()` exists and is the right wiring point (`lib/prompts/autopilot-kickoff.js`, served at `GET /api/proxy/autopilot/kickoff`), and already carries the compressed seed the manual expands ('You've run this loop before…' + 'How a loop goes' + 'When to halt'). `docs/autopilot-experiment.md` still contains runs B1–B4 and the Stage-A Runs 1–10 punch-list. The ticket's named episodes (B4 false-positive `[done]`, B2 halt-on-infra) are accurate.

**Source inventory.** Episode-level detail lives in: `autopilot-experiment.md` (richest — B1–B4 + Stage-A telemetry arc), `recommender-structural-drift.md` (the **HAR-527** boot-hang spiral — canonical drift episode), Linear **LIN-296** (wrong-altitude routing, Canceled), and the **LIN-319/320/321/318** churn cluster. Abstract framing (the principles/taxonomy behind the known-issues): `autopilot.md` (4 invariants, `kind`-trajectory), `drift-at-every-altitude.md` (the altitude through-line), `drift-defense.md`/LIN-289 (the heavier design this manual replaces), `recommender-failure-patterns.md`. Note: **HAR-527 is not in this Linear workspace** — it is a historical episode from another project, documented only in the drift docs + LIN-289's motivation; cite by name, no Linear ID.

**Retro-lens worked example (calibration sample).** Ran it over the `/recommend` 504 reliability cluster — a small in-project echo of the HAR-527 shape. Across B2/B3/B3-continuation, `/recommend` 504'd 4×+ on a *trivial* ticket; each run attributed it to 'Linear slowness' (locally plausible, repeated → the drift). A deliberate live probe split the legs (`/me` 0.86s, `/issues` 0.64s, `/recommend` **50.5s→504**) and found the real cause: the **OpenRouter generation leg**, masked by a `withTimeout()` helper hardcoding a Linear-flavoured error. Fix one altitude up: a dedicated `LLM_TIMEOUT_MS=180s` split (LIN-320, Done). **Retro verdict:** keep-going was right per run, but the cluster needed a reorient — *a repeated identical failure with a repeated identical explanation is itself the drift signal.* This is the entry shape every known-issue should take: what it looks like → named episode → keep-going/reorient/restart/escalate.

**Three gaps flagged (not papered over):**
1. **Worker-failure escalation has no episode** — B2–B4 only exercised the infra-error halt + evidence-contradiction flag, never a clean task-level `[failed]`/stall driving the `help` branch.
2. **No genuinely unattended run** — B1–B4 were all supervised; B4 *needed* a human observation to terminate.
3. **The autopilot-native drift sensor has never fired in-loop** — drift is grounded historically (HAR-527) + the misdiagnosis cluster, but B1–B4 all converged, so the `kind`-trajectory looping/sprawling read has no episode of catching live drift yet.

Episode→known-issue map, the section-level structure, the wiring approach, and the Surface Assessment are appended to the description for the plan/draft step. Full detail in the research notes doc.
